'''Daniel Kráľ''' (born June 30, 1978) is a Czech mathematician and computer scientist who works as a professor of mathematics and computer science at the [[Masaryk University]]. His research primarily concerns [[graph theory]] and graph [[algorithm]]s.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://www.ucw.cz/~kral/cv.html|title=Curriculum vitae: Daniel Kráľ|access-date=2015-09-17}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
He obtained his Ph.D. from [[Charles University in Prague]] in 2004, under the supervision of [[Jan Kratochvíl]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=127883}}</ref> After short-term positions at [[TU Berlin]], Charles University, and the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], he returned to Charles University as a researcher in 2006, and became a tenured associate professor there in 2010. He was awarded the degree of [[Doctor of Science]] by the [[Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic]] in 2012, and in the same year moved to a professorship at the [[University of Warwick]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{citation|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/dcs/news/?newsItem=094d43a23a44de64013a747c61b117c2|title=Daniel Kral joins the Department of Computer Science as a new Professor|publisher=University of Warwick Department of Computer Science|date=October 18, 2012|access-date=2015-09-17}}.</ref>

In 2018, Kráľ moved back to the Czech Republic and started working at Faculty of Informatics, [[Masaryk University]], accepting the Donald Knuth professorship chair.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://is.muni.cz/osoba/44742?lang=en | title=Personal Page prof. RNDR. Daniel Kráľ, Ph.D., DSC }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.respekt.cz/tydenik/2020/3/kral-diskretnich-cisel|title=Král diskrétních čísel|last=Svobodová|first=Ivana|website=Týdeník Respekt|access-date=2020-01-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ucw.cz/~kral/index.html.cs|title=Dan Král|website=www.ucw.cz|access-date=2020-01-14}}</ref>

==Contributions==
{{Scholia}}
In the 1970s, [[Michael D. Plummer]] and [[László Lovász]]
conjectured that every [[Bridge (graph theory)|bridgeless]] [[cubic graph]] has an exponential number of [[perfect matching]]s, strengthening [[Petersen's theorem]] that at least one perfect matching exists. In a pair of papers with different sets of co-authors, Kráľ was able to show that this conjecture is true.<ref>{{citation

 | last2 = Sereni | first2 = Jean-Sébastien
 | last3 = Stiebitz | first3 = Michael
 | doi = 10.1137/080723843

 | mr = 2556543

 | volume = 23

 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation

==Recognition==
Kráľ won first place and a gold medal at the [[International Olympiad in Informatics]] in 1996.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ioinformatics.org/locations/ioi96/results.shtml|title=The Final Results of IOI'96|publisher=[[International Olympiad in Informatics]]|access-date=2015-09-17}}.</ref>

In 2011, Kráľ won the [[European Prize in Combinatorics]] for his work in graph theory, particularly citing his solution to the Plummer–Lovász conjecture and his results on [[graph coloring]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://mta.hu/matematika_hirek/a-kombinatorika-kivalosagai-az-akademian-128508|title=A kombinatorika kiválóságai az Akadémián|publisher=[[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]|language=hu|date=September 1, 2011|access-date=2015-09-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131106013006/http://mta.hu/matematika_hirek/a-kombinatorika-kivalosagai-az-akademian-128508|archive-date=November 6, 2013}}.</ref> In 2014, he won a [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] in Mathematics and Statistics; the award citation again included Kráľ's research on the Plummer–Lovász conjecture, as well as other publications of Kráľ on [[pseudorandom]] [[permutation]]s and systems of equations.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/sites/default/files/imported_pdfs/2014-plp-citations.pdf|access-date=2015-09-17|title=Philip Leverhulme Prizes 2014|publisher=The Leverhulme Trust|archive-date=2018-02-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180207122152/https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/sites/default/files/imported_pdfs/2014-plp-citations.pdf}}.</ref>

He was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 Class, for "contributions to extremal combinatorics and graph theory, and for service to the profession".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2020 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2019-11-03}}</ref>
